html:
Air raids by British and American bombers on the German city of Dresden on 13 to 15 February 1945, which set off a firestorm and killed about 25,000 people.

Two waves of RAF Lancasters struck on the night of 13 February, using high explosive and fire bombs. The fires merged into one storm that pulled in air and burned the old city centre. American bombers followed the next two days. The city was crowded with refugees fleeing the Red Army.

Dresden was a rail and industrial centre, but also a famous baroque city with few defences. Many people have since asked whether the raid was needed so late in World War II. Nazi propaganda inflated the toll, and a historians' commission in 2010 settled on up to 25,000 dead.

The American writer Kurt Vonnegut survived as a prisoner of war and wrote about it in Slaughterhouse-Five. Compare the atomic bombings of Japan six months later.
sum: Air raids by British and American bombers on the German city of Dresden on 13 to 15 February 1945, which set off a firestorm and killed about 25,000 people.
